title: Role — Traefik
description: Any service's Traefik reverse proxy: availability, traffic, latency, routers and backend services, entrypoints and open connections, certificate expiry and configuration reloads. Pick the service (and optionally hosts) at the top; links can pass ?var-service=<name>.

panels.title: Availability
panels.description: Share of requests through this service's routers that did NOT end in a 5xx, over the selected time range.

panels.title: Requests / s
panels.description: Requests per second through every router of this service's proxy.

panels.title: 5xx (range)
panels.description: Server errors answered over the selected range.

panels.title: p95 latency
panels.description: 95th percentile of request duration at the proxy, upstream included. Traefik's default buckets are coarse (0.1, 0.3, 1.2, 5 s), so read it as a band, not a measurement.

panels.title: TLS cert expires in
panels.description: Days until the soonest-expiring certificate Traefik serves (the newest one per CN). ACME renews at 30 days left, so under ~25 means renewal is failing.

panels.title: Services down
panels.description: Backend services with no upstream server Traefik's health check holds up. One idle colour of a blue-green pair is not counted: only a service with none up is. Services without a health check report nothing, so the panel shows no data where none has one.

panels.title: Requests by status class
panels.description: Requests per second by status class. 0xx is Traefik's code 0: the client went away before a response.

panels.title: Latency (proxy)
panels.description: Request duration percentiles at Traefik, TLS termination to the upstream's last byte, interpolated within coarse buckets.

panels.title: Errors by status code
panels.description: 4xx, 5xx and aborted (0) requests per code. 401/404 storms are usually clients and crawlers; 5xx are the upstream's (or Traefik's 502/504 when it cannot reach it).

panels.title: Bandwidth
panels.description: Bytes served to and received from clients through the routers.

panels.title: Requests by method & protocol
panels.description: Request mix by HTTP method and protocol (http, websocket, sse).

panels.title: Routers (selected range)
panels.description: Every router over the selected range: mean request rate, share of 5xx and 4xx, and p95 latency.

targets.expr: (sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host", code=~"5.."}[$__range])) or sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range]))

(sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host", code=~"4.."}[$__range])) or sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Requests per router
panels.description: Request rate per router.

panels.title: 5xx ratio per router
panels.description: Share of each router's requests that ended in a 5xx; routers without errors are left out.

targets.expr: (sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host", code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0

panels.title: p95 latency per router
panels.description: 95th percentile request duration per router.

panels.title: Requests per service
panels.description: Requests Traefik forwarded to each backend service (Traefik's own service, not service_name).

panels.title: 5xx ratio per service
panels.description: Share of each backend's responses that were 5xx.

targets.expr: (sum by (service) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host", code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (service) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0) / sum by (service) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total{service_name="$service", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0

panels.title: p95 latency per service
panels.description: 95th percentile of the time the backend took, as Traefik measured it.

panels.title: Backend servers
panels.description: Each upstream server and whether Traefik's health check holds it up. Only services with a health check are listed (none means no health checks configured).

panels.title: Backend servers up
panels.description: Healthy upstream servers per service over time. A blue-green service shows 1, briefly 2 during a flip; 0 is an outage.

panels.title: Requests per entrypoint
panels.description: HTTP requests per entrypoint, including those no router matched (which never show in the router panels).

panels.title: Open connections
panels.description: Connections currently open per entrypoint, TCP passthrough entrypoints (mail, …) included. The metrics entrypoint is left out: that is the collector itself.

panels.title: TLS versions
panels.description: TLS requests by protocol version.

panels.title: Certificates
panels.description: Days until the newest certificate for each CN expires, soonest first. Traefik also reports certificates still in its store for names it no longer serves.

panels.title: Configuration reloads
panels.description: Dynamic configuration reloads per host (a deploy, a certificate renewal, a file-provider change). Traefik v3 exports no failed-reload counter; a failed reload shows as the 'since last successful reload' age not resetting.

panels.title: Since last successful reload
panels.description: Time since Traefik last applied a configuration without error. Long is normal on a quiet host; it matters when a change was just deployed and this did not reset.
